From a paper to a position.

What GaussVM implements, where it diverges, and what the tests establish.

What is an Aqua app?

Aqua is 1inch’s shared liquidity layer. A liquidity provider authorizes a trading strategy while keeping its tokens in their own wallet. An Aqua app supplies the trading rules and uses Aqua to settle transfers when a trade executes.

Here, GaussVM is the Aqua app: our SwapVM extension prices this market’s YES/NO swaps with the Gaussian pm-AMM rule. Aqua records the maker’s allocation and transfers the tokens. The separate BinaryMarket contract creates the collateral-backed outcomes and handles manual resolution.

For example, buying YES pays NO to the maker and receives YES from the maker. Shipping a liquidity position allocates those tokens without depositing them into Aqua. Maker funds must remain available for the swap to settle.

All saved liquidity positions use this one market and the same YES/NO tokens. They are pricing strategies, not additional markets.

Outcome tokens need a different model.

A YES token pays one unit of collateral if the event resolves YES; a NO token pays it otherwise. Their behavior near resolution differs from ordinary assets. Paradigm’s pm-AMM models this with Gaussian score dynamics and allocates liquidity accordingly.

Read Moallemi & Robinson’s original research
The static invariant
z = (y − x) / L
(y − x) Φ(z) + L φ(z) − y = 0

x and y are complementary outcome reserves. L is the liquidity scale. Φ is the normal CDF; φ is its density. GaussVM numerically solves the invariant for exact-input swaps.

One instruction. Official settlement.
Ship a strategy
The maker approves Aqua and records token allocations. No deposit occurs.
Run the Gaussian instruction
SwapVM executes opcode 0x80, validates the pair and expiry, and computes output.
Settle the trade
Official Aqua pull/push logic transfers tokens and updates the allocation. A Swapped event provides the receipt.
Boundaries are part of the implementation.
Exact input only, in either direction. Exact output reverts.
The numerical domain is |z| ≤ 3. Trading stops 60 seconds before expiry.
Time scaling preserves the current invariant level and retains inactive complete sets. It is an extension, not a verified implementation of every economic result in the paper.
Manual resolution is trusted. The test collateral is faucet-minted and has no monetary value.
The code is unaudited. Numerical tests do not prove economic safety, profitability or fitness for real funds.
Reproduce the evidence.

git submodule update --init --recursive
npm run check
npm run dev

# In a second terminal
npm run demo

The demo writes transaction receipts, event logs and before/after balances to reports/demo.json. Local hashes belong to your local chain and will not appear on a public explorer.
